key_insight: Algorithmic differentiation makes DFPT practical for meta-GGA exchange-correlation functionals by computing needed second derivatives as Jacobian-vector products instead of hand-derived formulas.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate and flexible response-property calculations and supports gradient-based training of new density functionals in electronic-structure workflows.
method: Extend DFPT to meta-GGA XC functionals Exc(ρ,τ) with explicit kinetic-energy-density dependence.
Recast XC second derivatives as Jacobian-vector products and evaluate them with algorithmic differentiation.
Integrate with AD-DFPT to obtain derivatives of arbitrary ground-state quantities under arbitrary perturbations.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on ZnO and BaTiO3 response properties and on training a neural-network meta-GGA to match hybrid-DFT silicon densities, with r2SCAN01 generally outperforming LDA and PBE in the reported tests.
watch_item: The implementation depends on accurate AD support for the XC functional and careful handling of self-consistency, which may add complexity for large-scale or highly customized functionals.
paper_title: Density functional perturbation theory of meta-generalized gradient approximations using algorithmic differentiation
